title: Camera inspection of filled vials
description:
Short title
Camera inspection of filled vials

What should the AI do?
A camera system with a trained neural network inspects every filled vial on the fill-finish line and automatically rejects vials with particles, cracks or a wrong fill level.

Where will it be used?
Manufacturing / production

Does the AI output directly affect a batch, a GMP record, a QC result, a release or a process setting?
Yes, directly. It makes the accept or reject decision for each vial.

What kind of AI is it?
Trained model, frozen: same input, same result. The model is locked after validation. Updates come as a new, validated version.

What happens with the output?
Used automatically; people spot-check or watch trends and alerts. Rejected vials go straight to the reject bin.

Who checks the output, and how?
Operators check the reject rate every shift; QA reviews rejects during batch record review.

Does the AI replace or reduce a check or step that people do today?
Yes, a step is dropped or reduced. It replaces the manual visual inspection of every vial.

What data goes into it?
Confidential company data

Who provides it?
Bought from a supplier, installed with us

verdict.label: GMP-critical ML: proceed with full controls (Annex 22)
verdict.explanation: A static, deterministic model in a critical GMP application is what draft Annex 22 covers. It is acceptable with the full Annex 22 lifecycle on top of Annex 11.

required_controls.title: Intended use and input sample space
required_controls.what: Describe the task, the input data with common and rare variations, subgroups and known limitations. A process SME approves it before acceptance testing.

required_controls.title: Test metrics and acceptance criteria
required_controls.what: Define case-dependent metrics (e.g. confusion matrix, sensitivity, specificity) and acceptance criteria approved by an SME; performance at least as good as the process it replaces.

required_controls.title: Representative, correctly labelled test data
required_controls.what: Test data covers the full sample space and subgroups, is large enough for statistical confidence, labels are independently verified; no generative-AI-generated test data without justification.

required_controls.title: Test-data independence
required_controls.what: Technical and procedural controls so test data is never used in training or validation, with access control and audit trail on the test set.

required_controls.title: Approved test plan and documented execution
required_controls.what: An approved test plan before testing; deviations documented and justified; test documentation retained as GMP documentation.

required_controls.title: Explainability and feature review
required_controls.what: Record which features drove each classification during testing (e.g. SHAP, LIME, heat maps) and review them as part of approving the results.

required_controls.title: Confidence scores and 'undecided' threshold
required_controls.what: Log a confidence score per prediction during testing (§9.1) and set an operational threshold below which the outcome is flagged 'undecided' (§9.2).

required_controls.title: Change and configuration control of the model
required_controls.what: Put the tested model, its system and the process under change and configuration control; evaluate every change for retest; detect unauthorised changes.

required_controls.title: Performance and input-drift monitoring
required_controls.what: Monitor model performance and whether inputs stay within the tested sample space, with defined drift metrics.

required_controls.title: Documented quality risk assessment
required_controls.what: A justified, documented risk assessment sets the extent of validation and data-integrity controls; formality proportional to risk.
sources: ICH Q9(R1) §5.1 Formality in Quality Risk Management

required_controls.title: Computerised system validation
required_controls.what: Validate the application and qualify the infrastructure, scaled to risk; keep it in a validated state through its lifecycle.

required_controls.title: Data integrity (ALCOA+)
required_controls.what: Data the system captures, processes or reports must be trustworthy (ALCOA+); assess data criticality with QRM; the regulated user stays accountable for records produced with AI.

required_controls.title: Audit trail
required_controls.what: Record GMP-relevant user interactions: creation, change and deletion of data with user, time and reason (Annex 11). This tool's recommendation for AI systems: also log inputs, model and prompt versions and outputs.

required_controls.title: Supplier and service-provider oversight
required_controls.what: Formal agreements, supplier audit and ongoing oversight; review supplier documentation for externally provided models. For hosted AI services, agree how new model versions are released and whether you can test them before release.

required_controls.title: AI use inside the pharmaceutical quality system
required_controls.what: Include the AI support in the PQS (on premise or hosted); the regulated user stays accountable for the integrity of records produced with AI.

required_controls.title: Periodic review
required_controls.what: Review the system periodically after go-live to verify it stays in a validated state and fit for its intended use.

required_controls.title: Roles, qualification and training
required_controls.what: Defined responsibilities and adequate training for everyone using or maintaining the system; AI literacy for staff using AI.
sources: EU AI Act: Article 4: AI literacy

required_controls.title: US products: FDA credibility assessment
required_controls.what: For products under FDA oversight, model outputs that support regulatory decisions (including actions taken under CGMP, per the draft guidance's scope) call for FDA's risk-based credibility framework: question of interest, context of use, model risk (influence × consequence), credibility plan.
sources: FDA AI credibility guidance (draft) §IV.A A risk-based credibility assessment framework
FDA AI credibility guidance (draft) §IV.A.3 Step 3: Assess the AI model risk

required_controls.title: EU AI Act screening
required_controls.what: Check whether the system is high-risk (Art. 6, Annex III; e.g. AI used in recruitment or worker management) and, if so, meet the deployer duties of Art. 26. Ensure AI literacy of staff (Art. 4). Transparency duties (Art. 50) fall mainly on the provider; as deployer, check they are met.
sources: EU AI Act: Article 6: Classification rules for high-risk AI systems
EU AI Act: Annex III: High-risk AI systems referred to in Article 6(2)
EU AI Act: Article 26: Obligations of deployers of high-risk AI systems
EU AI Act: Article 4: AI literacy
EU AI Act: Article 50: Transparency obligations for providers and deployers of certain AI systems

sources.quote: This annex applies to all types of computerised systems used in the manufacturing of medicinal products and active substances, where Artificial Intelligence models are used in critical applications with direct impact on patient safety, product quality or data integrity, e.g. to predict or classify data.
The document applies to static models, i.e. models that do not adapt their performance during use by incorporating new data.

sources.ref: FDA AI credibility guidance (draft) §IV.A.2 Step 2: Define the context of use for the AI model
sources.quote: Therefore, the AI-based model will not be the sole determinant for the release of product (the AI model’s scope).
